chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed a fox; he said, 'Upon him is the blood-price (damm).' I said, 'And an arnab (a type of hare/rabbit)?' He said, 'Like what is in the fox.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah; a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.أَرْنَباً: An arnab; a type of hare or rabbit, often distinguished from the common rabbit in classical texts.
key_terms.ثَعْلَباً: A fox; a specific wild animal mentioned in the hadith.
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood-price; compensation paid for killing an animal or person, often in cases of error.

ai.seo_question: What is the blood-price (damm) for accidentally killing a fox or arnab in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific blood-price (*damm*) for accidentally killing a fox or an *arnab* (often identified as the hare or rabbit), establishing their equivalence in legal valuation. This ruling highlights the detailed jurisprudential framework within Shia fiqh regarding *kaffarah* (expiation) for the *muhrim* (one in Hajj/Umrah state) who transgresses hunting prohibitions, distinguishing between different species based on their perceived value or status. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how specific animal types are categorized in the calculation of compensatory sacrifices during the sacred months.
